messages:
marcus: Heads-up: payments customer asking for a BYO-HSM POC. Must-have: offline key ceremony, signed import receipts, 30d rotation, and cryptographic dual-control during rotation. Can we scope a POC runbook?
jia: Yes. Private connector supports PKCS#11 imports and can surface attestation blobs. For dual-control we usually rely on vendor/customer-side multi-signer support; Redwood can enforce a two-operator approval step via an API/webhook before executing rotation.
talia: Compliance asks for signed import receipts, MAA/attestation artifacts, and tamper-seal photos for the HSM crate. Also require forwarding all import/key events to their SIEM.
ops-bot: FYI connector-v2 rolling deploy tonight (canary). No customer-impact expected.
marcus: Latency ask: <=60ms p50 for key unwrap in inference path. They're modelling ~200M inference calls/month. How do we avoid HSM QPS explosion while meeting latency?
jia: Best practice: envelope encryption with short-lived DEKs cached in-memory on inference nodes. If DEK TTL = 600s (10m) you'd reduce HSM lookups dramatically. If they insist on stricter limits we can set TTL shorter and use proactive rotation webhooks to invalidate caches immediately on rotation.
talia: They require DEK TTL <=10m and that DEKs are not persisted beyond process lifetime. Also must support immediate revocation via an invalidation webhook.
marcus: Geo-redundancy: they want deterministic routing and mirrored HSM between eu-west-1 and us-east-1. We need a clear failover plan.
jia: We can deploy Private connectors in both regions and set routing policy to primary -> secondary. Synchronous HSM mirroring is a vendor feature; we will document options (sync vs async) and include the deterministic failover steps in the runbook.
legal-bot: Pricing note: BYO-HSM has onboarding + per-HSM-op pricing. For 200M calls/mo, with DEK caching we'd expect far fewer HSM lookups (ballpark 1-3M lookups/day). Rough est: fixed onboarding + ~$0.000015 per lookup. Will produce a formal quote.
marcus: Offline ceremony flow (they want exact steps we will follow) — can we list a concise import flow?
jia: Flow: 1) Customer generates key material offline and produces vendor import bundle. 2) Customer wraps/encrypts per vendor import spec and transfers bundle to us over mutual TLS. 3) Upload to Redwood Private import API (staging). 4) Connector executes PKCS#11/vendor import; connector captures attestation blob. 5) Redwood writes signed import receipt + timestamp and forwards audit bundle to customer S3/SIEM.
talia: Add: dual-signature requirement for the import package (operator A prepares, operator B approves). Also capture tamper-evidence photos and store them with the audit bundle.
marcus: Fallback/HA: customer wants automatic fallback to Redwood-managed keys only if HSM unreachable, with a 45m cooldown and explicit customer opt-in. Allowed?
talia: Allowed, but must be explicit in the SOW and toggled only with written approval. All fallback events must be logged, alerted, and auditable. No silent fallback.
marcus: Can someone drop a minimal SOW blurb and a sample config snippet I can send to the customer for the POC?
jia: SOW paragraph (minimal): "Redwood will provision a Private connector to integrate the customer's HSM using PKCS#11. Redwood will support an import ceremony for customer-generated key material, capture attestation blobs, and forward signed import receipts and audit logs to the customer's audit sink. Rotation orchestration is supported; dual-control approval is enforced via a two-operator approval step triggered by the customer. Fallback to Redwood-managed keys is available only with explicit customer authorization and is auditable."
jia: Sample POC config (replace placeholders):
```
external_kms:
  provider: customer_hsm
  connector: private-agent-v2
  pkcs11_module: /opt/hsm/lib/vendor_pkcs11.so
  key_id: projects/payments/keys/txn-llm
  key_wrapping: rsa-oaep-sha256
  rotation_days: "30"
  dek_ttl_seconds: "600"   # 10m
  allow_fallback: false
```
marcus: Great. Also need POC checklist: ports, mTLS cert exchange steps, test vectors (envelope encrypt/unwrapping), timeline (2-week POC).
talia: I'll produce a checklist and runbook: network diagram, mutual TLS cert exchange, required ports (outbound 443 to vendor endpoints + our collector), sample test vectors for envelope flow, and an acceptance test plan.
ops-bot: Scheduling note: private-agent-v2 will join the canary pool tonight.
legal-bot: Posted initial pricing note to internal quote: https://redwood.example.com/sales/byo-hsm-quote-190123 (internal).
marcus: Thanks all. Once checklist + SOW + pricing are attached I'll schedule the customer call. :thumbsup:
